modifiers.H: lenite toward /h/ — spirantize consonants (sH→ʃ, tH→θ); vowels lax (iH→ɪ, uH→ʊ) or, for a, back (aH→ɑ)
modifiers.Y: central — the y-vowels (iY→ɨ, uY→ʉ, eY→ɘ, oY→ɵ); Welsh y, Russian ы
modifiers.C: click — base letter is the anterior place (p bilabial, t dental, q alveolar, c palatal, l lateral)
modifiers.X: ejective (voiceless glottalic egressive; voiceless obstruents only)

COMBINING BREVE (extra-short; ⇧ → the breve BELOW, U+032F — the non-syllabic mark, which IS an inverted breve below. It used to sit on ⌥⇧s, where it had no claim on the key beyond adjacency to `syllabic`; the breve key is its shape's home. Vacating ⌥⇧s is what let the syllabic line have its own second placement. The two stack — a segment can be both extra-short and non-syllabic)

Placement carries no meaning — it is typography, and it is the transcriber's. The ring sits in THIS plane because that is where ABC Extended puts its ring key, and muscle memory beat a weak frequency edge; it is also what makes å one modifier again: ⌥k then a)

superscripts.rule: Generated, not curated: a glyph superscripts iff Unicode defines a modifier letter (Lm) or superscript digit (No) whose compatibility decomposition is <super> of it. Exceptions ʔ→ˀ and ʕ→ˤ have no decomposition. Latin Extended-F forms (U+10780+, Unicode 14) are excluded — correct but near-universally tofu. One further exception: bare `g` is U+0067 for the plain-US constraint, but it stands for IPA ɡ (U+0261), so it superscripts to ᶢ (ɡ's form), not ᵍ.

laws.optShift: ⌥ gives a mark's primary form, ⌥⇧ its `double`. ⌥⇧ has no single meaning: see `classes.shiftSense` for the six, and `classes.exclusive` for whether a pair replaces or stacks. Both are recorded per-mark.
laws.keyClasses: A key earns its mark by cross-tier phonetics, by shape identity (the comma key carries the comma-shaped marks; the period key the dot-shaped ones), or by convention (the five universal dead keys ⌥e ⌥i ⌥u ⌥n ⌥`). Where none of the three applies the mark is parked and flagged `arbitraryKey`. Marks outside the IPA are flagged `ipa: false`; see `classes.beyond`.
laws.numberRow: ⇧<digit> carries an IPA glyph with no Latin home (⇧2 ʔ, ⇧5 ə). The one exception is the tie bar on ⇧6 — a combining joiner (t ⇧6 s → t͡s), contrastive and frequent, so it earns a single-modifier key. It lives on the number row, not on a ⇧-letter, because an unguarded ⇧-letter joiner would fire inside acronyms ($PATH). Because ⇧6 is thereby claimed, its raw-US ^ moves to the option-shift escape, exactly as @ sits on the ⇧2 escape.
laws.placement: A mark's PLACEMENT is the transcriber's, never the engine's. Three marks have both an above- and a below-form — the tie bar (⇧6, press again to flip), the voiceless ring (⌥k below, ⌥⇧k above), and the syllabic line (⌥s below, ⌥⇧s above) — and the engine used to choose two of them by looking the base up in a hardcoded set of glyphs-with-descenders. That is a TYPOGRAPHY model inside a NOTATION engine, and it failed both ways: it silently pushed an explicit ring back below, so å — a LETTER, not a diacritic — could not be typed at all; and the descender set had drifted, missing ɲ ʎ ɸ β ç ʑ and ɧ, so it buried rings in their tails regardless. That class of bug is invisible in review, because the codepoint is right and only the rendering collides. The set is deleted. Every placement is now one keystroke, and the engine emits exactly the mark you asked for.
laws.tieBar: ⇧6 is the tie ABOVE (U+0361, t͡s). The chart also sanctions the tie BELOW (U+035C) for when descenders collide with a bar above — t͜ɕ, d͜ʒ, k͜p — and it is the same mark, not a second one. So it gets no key: press ⇧6 AGAIN while a tie sits before the cursor and it flips, above ⇄ below. Stateless (the document holds the tie, not the engine), reversible, and it spends no keyboard real estate, which is the only reason the below-form fits at all.
laws.scriptG: IPAbet types g as U+0067, not U+0261 LATIN SMALL LETTER SCRIPT G. The IPA sanctions both shapes and every IPA font draws them alike, but U+0261 is the codepoint the chart specifies — so this is a deliberate, known non-conformance, bought by the bare-layer law (an unshifted key is native US, and the native g key is U+0067). It is invisible to a reader and visible to a grep: corpus work that diffs against reference transcriptions must normalize. U+0261 still appears in the tables as a lookup key (superscripts, descenders), so text pasted in with a script g behaves correctly.
laws.dashes: ⌥- and ⌥⇧- (en/em dash) are never overridden. This is why advanced/retracted live on ⌥=.
laws.punctuation: The host's orthographic punctuation is reserved, like the dashes. ⌥[ ⌥] ⌥\ carry “ ” ‘ ’ « » and ⌥⇧/ carries ¿ — these keys are never claimed. An unassigned ⌥<key> passes to the host, digits included, so its typography survives. An ⌥⇧<digit> escapes to raw US only where ⇧<digit> is an IPA glyph; otherwise it passes or is spent deliberately (see `optShift`).
laws.escape: ⇧<letter> transforms the glyph before it, so a capital that forms a digraph is otherwise untypeable ("GitHub" → "Giθub"). ⌃⇧<letter> is the escape: it commits the raw capital and bypasses everything downstream — the ⇧-modifier transforms, the shift-chain, the capital-digraph rule — so ⌃⇧G ⌃⇧H is a literal "GH" and ⌃⇧A ⌃⇧E a literal "AE". It sits on Control because Control is inert here: ⌃ chords are leader keys (tmux ^b, emacs ^x) and pass untouched, and ⌃⇧<letter> is a chord almost no host claims. Letters only — ⌃⇧<digit/punct> keeps its native chord. Moving the escape here freed the whole ⌥⇧<letter> layer, which formerly had to hold it and so could never be spent freely. ⌥⇧<digit> is a different job: reachability, not escaping (⇧2 is ʔ, so @ lives on ⌥⇧2).
laws.capsLock: Caps Lock is a LOCK, not a modifier. The bare layer is native US and Caps Lock belongs to it: a letter types its CAPITAL, literally. It never acts as ⇧ (a locked T then H is "TH", not θ), and the capital it types is inert text downstream — the modifier tables are lowercase-keyed — which is the same acronym safety ⌃⇧ relies on. ⇧ still means the modifier while locked, and a pending mark still absorbs onto the capital (⌥u then a locked A → Ä).
laws.planes: WHICH form of a pair gets the unshifted ⌥ key, and which gets ⌥⇧. In priority order: (1) DON'T FIGHT THE HOST — if the mark exists on ABC Extended, keep its key AND its plane; Mac muscle memory is an asset we did not build and cannot buy, and violating it costs every user forever (this is why the voiceless ring defaults ABOVE, against a weak frequency edge, and why the cedilla is on ⌥c). (2) FREQUENCY — the form you type more often is unshifted (long ː over half-long ˑ, primary stress over secondary, syllabic-below over syllabic-above). (3) PRECEDENCE — when frequency is a wash and the pair has a natural order, the opening/first/lesser member is unshifted: “ before ”, ‘ before ’, « before », – before —, acute before double-acute. (4) IPA OVER TENANT — where an IPA mark and a Latin-orthography tenant want the same slot, the IPA meaning wins the unshifted plane, unless (1) says otherwise. Key CHOICE is a separate question with its own rules — see keyClasses.
laws.arbitraryKeys: A mark with no claim on its key — neither phonetics, shape, nor convention — is flagged `arbitraryKey`, and it must sit on an UNEARNED slot: one whose native macOS character no law defends and nobody needs (ª º ∆ ¶ § ÷ ®). An arbitrary mark on a valuable key is the worst of both worlds — it teaches nothing and it costs something. The horn used to break this rule, parked on an arbitrary letter key while destroying ¥; it moved to ⌥7, where Vietnamese VNI convention justifies it (ơ = o7) and the slot was worthless, and ¥ came back. Three marks remain arbitrary — linguolabial ⌥9, unreleased ⌥j, Korean fortis ⌥0 — and all three destroy only ª ∆ º.

classes.about: Definitions for the flags carried by entries in `marks`. Membership lives on each mark, never in this prose — a key can be reassigned without editing a word here.
classes.ipa: Absent or true: the mark is on the official IPA chart, and appears on /chart and /chart.json. `false`: it is not, and `beyond` names the tradition it answers to. Non-IPA marks are fully typeable and are listed on /keys.

beyond.tenant: Not IPA and never was. Carried so the layout can also write real Latin orthographies and romanizations — Romanian, Vietnamese, Polish, German, Semitic transliteration. Tenants cohabit with IPA marks on the Option layer; they are not their neighbours' pairs.
beyond.tradition: Standard within a phonological tradition but absent from the IPA chart — e.g. the Korean fortis mark. Real notation, wrong chart.

classes.arbitraryKey: The key claims the mark by neither phonetics, shape, nor convention. Assigned to a mediocre reach and labelled arbitrary rather than given a fake mnemonic.

shiftSense.about: What ⌥⇧ means for a mark that has a `double`. The sense is a property of the pair, not a single rule: six exist. Orthogonal to `exclusive`, which says whether the two forms replace each other.
shiftSense.greater: ⌥⇧ is the greater pole of one dimension: advanced, raised, more rounded, ATR, upstep.
shiftSense.extreme: ⌥⇧ is the more extreme value on a scale: extra-high, extra-low.
shiftSense.lesser: ⌥⇧ is the diminished value: secondary stress, half-long. The mirror of `greater`, and the reason ⌥⇧ cannot be read as 'more' alone.
shiftSense.below: ⌥⇧ is a DIFFERENT diacritic that shares this glyph's shape, sitting below the base: tilde/creaky, diaeresis/breathy, caron/voiced, dot/dot, breve/non-syllabic. The shape is a memory hook, not a meaning — ⌥⇧n is not 'a lower tilde', it is creaky voice.
shiftSense.twin: The two forms are independent — a shape or kin relation, no polarity. They stack. (ʿayn/hamza, undertie/‖.)
shiftSense.arbitrary: An unpolarized dual: the two forms are values of one dimension but neither is greater. Which one takes ⌥⇧ is a coin flip, and is labelled as such. (apical/laminal.)
shiftSense.placement: ⌥⇧ is the SAME mark on the other side of the base. The meaning is identical; placement is typography and the transcriber owns it (laws.placement). The direction differs per mark because each follows its own frequency: the ring defaults ABOVE (ŋ̊ j̊ ɡ̊, and ABC Extended's ring key), the syllabic line BELOW (n̩ l̩ m̩ r̩).

classes.exclusive: The two forms are values of the SAME dimension, so ⌥⇧ replaces rather than stacks — nothing is both advanced and retracted. Marks on INDEPENDENT dimensions stack (nasalized + creaky). Tone level is a five-way scale, so an exclusive pair need not be binary or exhaustive.

optShift.about: ⌥⇧<digit> normally escapes to the raw US character, because ⇧<digit> is claimed by an IPA glyph and would otherwise be unreachable (⌥⇧2 → @). Where ⇧<digit> is NOT claimed the escape is redundant, and the slot is free. These are the two we spend; the rest of the unclaimed slots (⌥⇧8 ⌥⇧9 ⌥⇧0) pass to the host so its ° · ‚ survive.
